statement: A sequence is defined by $u_1=2$ and $u_{n+1}=3u_n-2$ for $n\ge 1$. Prove by induction that $u_n = 3^{n-1}+1$ for all $n\ge 1$.
solution:
Base case $n=1$: $3^{1-1}+1=1+1=2=u_1$, so the formula holds.

Inductive step: assume $u_k=3^{k-1}+1$ for some $k\ge 1$. Then
$$u_{k+1}=3u_k-2 = 3(3^{k-1}+1)-2 = 3^k+3-2 = 3^k+1 = 3^{(k+1)-1}+1.$$
So the formula holds for $k+1$. By induction it holds for all $n\ge 1$.
hints: Use the recurrence to get u_{k+1} = 3^k+1.
